content: Smart Finance and Digital Banking Lab Introduction The Smart Finance and Digital Banking Laboratory is established with the mission to conduct research, development, and application of advanced digital technologies in the finance and banking sectors. SFDB lab is a convergence of academia, business, government, and the community with the mission of becoming a leadership center for innovative research and application in the field of Fintech in Vietnam. SFDB lab was established to create a collaborative environment that encourages dialogue, experimentation, and innovation in digital banking, smart finance, and regulations related to digital assets and decentralized banking. The Lab is committed to generating new ideas that can help address complex and urgent challenges of Fintech, from promoting financial inclusion and improving access to financial services, from enhancing security and data privacy to reducing fraud, and from creating reliable digital infrastructure for the future of work and life as well as economic development. Research Direction ● Digital banking Digital transformation in firms, especially banking sectors, in provinces and in the economy Application of AI, blockchain to optimize users’ experience, operational management, risk management... ● Smart finance: Implementation of AI, blockchain to maximize user experience in diferent types of financial investment including personal finance (personal financial planning, retirement planning), corporate finance (risk management, financial analysis), financial investment (applications that help optimize investment portfolios, risk management... in securities, insurance companies...) Financial inclusion○ Sustainable development finance (green/sustainability finance, carbon credit trading markets...) ● Legal regulations related to digital assets and other innovative application of Fintech

content: Software Engineering and Decentralized Systems Lab Introduction In recent decades, decentralized systems have attracted significant attention from researchers, particularly in the field of software engineering. This growing interest has led to the exploration and application of software engineering technologies in the development of efficient, secure, and reliable decentralized systems. The Software Engineering and Decentralized Systems Lab was established to bring together researchers from both fields, with the aim of advancing decentralized technologies beyond their current limitations. Our group has a strong interest in blockchain — a prominent decentralized technology — and is therefore also known as the Blockchain Lab. Contact: dangtv@soict.hust.edu.vn (Dr. Tran Van Dang) Research Directions Our research interests include, but are not limited to: Blockchain Security: Developing algorithms to detect vulnerabilities in blockchain smart contracts and monitor on-chain decentralized applications. Decentralized Data Management: Developing novel frameworks for managing, synchronizing, and sharing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data across distributed systems. Data Analytics on Blockchain Networks: Designing data pipelines and analytical tools to process, store, and analyse data available on blockchain networks. Decentralized Technologies: Researching core blockchain technologies such as consensus algorithms, smart contract compilers and execution environments, etc. Research Problems Some key challenges that we are addressing include: Automated verification for smart contracts: Addressing the limitations of dynamic testing by leveraging static analysis to uncover bugs and vulnerabilities before deployment. Smart contract audit: Applying AI techniques to identify, explain, and repair bugs and vulnerabilities in smart contracts. Interoperability of decentralized data management systems: Developing platforms for decentralized data interoperability,

content: Operational Efficiency in Finance Lab Introduction The Operational Efficiency in Finance Laboratory (OEFin Lab) is a research facility established under the Institute for Digital Technology and Economy (BK Fintech), Hanoi University of Science and Technology. The laboratory focuses on optimization, applied mathematics, operational optimization, finance, and business applications. The development of information technology has triggered the digital transformation revolution in the financial sector and reshaped the competitive landscape of the banking industry. This transformation has profoundly affected the operational efficiency of many state-owned and commercial banks. The increasing banking competition has disrupted traditional market competitive structures, creating stronger impacts on banks' operational performance. The global financial industry is undergoing comprehensive integration of digital transformation technologies as well as adoption of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data, and the Internet of Things. This integration is driving a new technological revolution that is reshaping business operations. The digital transformation revolution in finance has promoted the digitization of traditional finance, with banks playing important roles in this process. Unlike traditional financial services that rely mainly on financial institutions and physical branches to conduct business operations, digital transformation in finance relies on online services, core digital technologies such as mobile payments and big data analytics, and has strong spatial and temporal independence. content: Học viên Giảng viên Doanh nghiệp Dành cho Học viên Phát triển kỹ năng an toàn thông tin từ học tập đến thực tế ĐĂNG KÝ NGAY Vườn ươm Nhân lực An toàn Thông tin tại Đại học Bách khoa Hà Nội hướng tới một môi trường học tập và thực hành giúp sinh viên: Học tập Trải nghiệm Phát triển Chứng nhận Cơ hội Phát triển Rèn luyện kỹ năng giao tiếp, làm việc nhóm, tư duy phản biện và tác phong chuyên nghiệp; đồng thời xây dựng định hướng nghề nghiệp trong môi trường công nghệ và chuyển đổi số. Chứng nhận Sinh viên hoàn thành chương trình sẽ được cấp chứng nhận đào tạo và ghi nhận quá trình tham gia các hoạt động học tập, thực hành và hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp. Cơ hội phát triển chuyên sâu Những học viên nổi bật có cơ hội tham gia các chương trình nâng cao, kết nối với mentor, chuyên gia và mở rộng định hướng nghề nghiệp trong lĩnh vực chuyển đổi số. Học tập Tiếp cận kiến thức về an toàn thông tin, quản trị rủi ro và bảo mật dữ liệu thông qua chương trình đào tạo kết hợp giữa lý thuyết, tình huống thực tế và học liệu số được xây dựng theo định hướng ứng dụng. Trải nghiệm Tham gia các hoạt động thực hành, phân tích tình huống và hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp trong quá trình chuyển đổi số dưới sự đồng

Doanh nghiệp có thể được hỗ trợ nâng cao nhận thức về an toàn thông tin, bảo mật dữ liệu, quản lý số và nhận diện các rủi ro cơ bản trong quá trình vận hành và chuyển đổi số. Hoạt động hỗ trợ được triển khai theo hình thức nào? Tùy theo điều kiện thực tế và nhu cầu của doanh nghiệp, hoạt động hỗ trợ có thể được triển khai trực tiếp tại doanh nghiệp hoặc trực tuyến thông qua nền tảng của chương trình. Doanh nghiệp có phải trả chi phí khi tham gia chương trình không? Không. Các hoạt động hỗ trợ trong khuôn khổ dự án được triển khai theo định hướng hỗ trợ cộng đồng và nâng cao năng lực cho doanh nghiệp tham gia chương trình. Bắt đầu hành trình của bạn trong lĩnh vực An toàn Thông tin ngay hôm nay! content: Business Intelligence Overview 1. Type: Short-term course 2. Format: Available in both Online and Offline (On-site) formats 3. Location (for offline classes): HUST-MB Digital Hub or Room 611, Blockchain R&D Center, 6th floor, Ta Quang Buu Library, Hanoi University of Science and Technology, 1st Dai Co Viet Street, Hanoi, Vietnam 4. Duration: 30 hours Training Schedule The schedule is designed to accommodate both students and working professionals: Time: 7:00 PM – 9:00 PM on weekdays Course length: 15 sessions (~2 months) plus 1 additional month for completing an individual project with feedback from both academic and industry instructors. Key Takeaways Upon completion of the course, participants will be able to: Understand the trends and applications of Business Intelligence (BI) in Economics, Finance, Marketing, and Logistics. Gain hands-on experience with leading BI tools such as Power BI and automation platforms including Power Automate, KNIME, and No-code AI solutions. Acquire essential BI data analysis techniques. Receive a Certificate of Completion issued by Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST). Faculty Academic Instructors The academic team consists of Associate Professors and PhD holders specializing in Information Technology and Finance. They bring strong academic backgrounds combined with applied research and real-world BI project experience. Industry Practitioners The practice-oriented team includes BI professionals with extensive hands-on expertise, directly involved in implementing Power BI and BI solutions at leading enterprises. Course Structure The Business Intelligence training program is designed with three modules: Module 1: Data-driven mindset and BI applications in enterprises Module 2: Data analysis techniques

Each issue spotlights key opportunities, introduces cutting-edge innovations, showcases emerging technology trends, and empowers businesses to make strategic decisions. More than just a publication, Vietnam Digital Economy Review is a dynamic platform for dialogue, innovation, and policy development —driving sustainable growth

content: Welcome Message: Shaping Vietnam's Digital Future On behalf of the Institute for Digital Technology and Economy at Hanoi University of Science and Technology, I extend my warmest welcome to you. We are living in one of the most dynamic periods of our nation's development. As a pioneering institution, our mission is to lead the digital transformation, master emerging technologies, and drive economic innovation in Vietnam. At the Institute, we do not just research—we create. From groundbreaking FinTech solutions to advanced digital economy models and transformative digital society initiatives, all our efforts are directed towards one goal: to contribute actively to the prosperity of Vietnam's digital economy and society. This commitment is built upon five core values: Innovation: Prioritizing creativity and innovation to always lead the way. Collaboration: Building strong bridges between academia, industry, and government. Excellence: Maintaining the highest standards in training, research, and development. Integrity: Upholding the highest ethical standards, transparency, and respect for diversity. Sustainability: Optimizing resources and aligning with sustainable development goals. With modern facilities and a team of leading experts, we are dedicated to nurturing high-quality human resources for the digital economy. We believe in the power of collaboration to shape the future. We look forward to the opportunity to create new value with you, contributing to our country's remarkable journey of development. Sincerely, Assoc. Prof. Nguyen Binh Minh, Ph.D. Dean Institute for Digital Technology and Economy Hanoi University of Science and Technology

content: Institute for Digital Technology and Economy and A-Star X Sign Memorandum of Understanding to Advance the Innovation Ecosystem On 24 July 2026, the Institute for Digital Technology and Economy at Hanoi University of Science and Technology and A-Star X officially signed a Memorandum of Understanding. The agreement marks a new milestone in the partnership between the two organisations, with a shared commitment to strengthening connections among education, research, product development and the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem. The signing ceremony was held as part of broader efforts to promote collaboration among universities, businesses and the technology community. Under the Memorandum of Understanding, the Institute for Digital Technology and Economy and A-Star X will collaborate on practice-oriented training programmes, research activities, professional workshops, mentoring initiatives, hackathons, product development and industry engagement. A key focus of the partnership is the joint operation and development of BKFintech Hackday and BKFintech Founder in Residence. These initiatives are designed to provide students, product development teams and aspiring founders with opportunities to address real-world challenges, receive guidance from experienced professionals and gradually transform their ideas into practical and scalable solutions. Connecting academic education with innovation practice As technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain and Web3 continue to reshape economic, financial and business activities, the requirements for technology professionals are extending beyond technical knowledge. Students and young builders must also develop problem-solving skills, interdisciplinary capabilities, product thinking and a strong understanding of market needs. Building a sustainable collaborative ecosystem The Institute for Digital Technology and Economy recognises that a sustainable innovation ecosystem cannot be created through a single competition, workshop or short-term initiative. Such an ecosystem requires long-term collaboration among universities, businesses, experts, founders, investors and the broader technology community. The signing of the Memorandum of Understanding with A-Star X provides a foundation for the two organisations to develop substantive and long-term programmes covering education, research, human resource development, product building, project incubation and market connectivity. Each activity implemented under the partnership will create further opportunities for students to learn, experiment and strengthen their capabilities as they gradually develop into future builders and founders. Following the signing, the Institute for Digital Technology and Economy and A-Star X will continue to translate the agreed areas of cooperation into specific initiatives, with an initial focus on the joint operation of BKFintech Hackday and BKFintech Founder in Residence. Both organisations expect these programmes to generate meaningful value for students, the technology community and the broader innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem.

content: Cyber Clinic Train-the-Trainer: Enhancing Lecturers’ Capacity to Support Businesses in the Digital Era As digital transformation continues to accelerate, the need to develop high-quality human resources in information security has become increasingly urgent. To help address this challenge, Hanoi University of Science and Technology is implementing the Cybersecurity Human Resources Incubator in the Digital Economy – Cyber Clinic project, with support from The Asia Foundation (TAF) and funding from Google.org. The project aims to establish and operate the Cyber Clinic as an incubator for training, support, and knowledge sharing in information security, while promoting lifelong learning for students, lecturers, businesses, and the wider community. It also focuses on training young professionals with technical expertise, practical skills, and advisory capabilities in information security, enabling them to support micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). The project is being implemented in several provinces and cities, including Hanoi, Quang Ninh, Dien Bien, Lao Cai, Thanh Hoa, Da Nang, and Can Tho. As one of the project’s key activities, the Train-the-Trainer Programme was held at the MB Digital Hub, with the participation of experts, lecturers, and representatives of partner organisations. The programme brought together leading experts in information security, law, and education to develop a team of lecturers with strong professional expertise and modern teaching methods. Directions for Information Security Workforce Development Delivering the opening remarks, Assoc. Prof. Huynh Quyet Thang, Vice President of Hanoi University of Science and Technology, emphasised the role of higher education institutions in training human resources to meet the demands

content: V-Chain Home V-Chain Exploding in early 2018, Blockchain has become one of the technologies that has changed the world. The development of technology, leading to the birth of many blockchain networks such as Ethereum, Hyperledger Fabric, Avalanche, etc., makes programmers need more time to research on technology and develop decentralized applications - this is also the reason for the birth of the V-Chain platform. What is V-Chain? V-Chain is a platform that supports programmers in developing and deploying decentralized applications on a variety of existing blockchain networks. Currently, the programming time for decentralized applications can last up to several months, but with V-Chain, this time can be shortened to just a few days. V-Chain allows users to easily define application operations, the roles of actors, as well as the data they want to write to a specific blockchain network. From there, V-Chain generates APIs/SDKs to support programmers in communicating with the blockchain network. The platform also supports the deployment of applications, or even a private blockchain network. Core Services The purpose of core services is to enable upper layers

content: node in the network themselves, or create a private blockchain to increase security and make transactions quickly. 2. Core Services The purpose of core services is to enable upper layers to communicate with underlying blockchain networks in a unified and easy way. Some notable core services include: Smart contract: V-Chain uses a common, consistent format for users to generate smart contracts for different blockchain platforms. Data model: defines a unified model for storing data on the blockchain network. Resource management: to connect and distribute resources to applications, and to keep logs from nodes, service and application read and write operations at upper layers. 3. Utility Services Utility services are developed to support the deployment of decentralized applications in companies, organizations and governments. The services will help blockchainize the organization's existing operations. Some of the services on the V-Chain platform currently include: V-Engine: Users can choose which blockchain network to record data on such as Hyperledger Fabric, Ethereum or IPFS, or create their own blockchain V-Mapping: Users define the data stored on the chain, the relationship between the data V-Trace: Users can retrieve data on the network and display it on their applications. V-Storage: is a decentralized storage service based on IPFS technology V-Monitoring: A service that helps users monitor the status of transactions, nodes and the entire blockchain network. V-Token: A service that automatically deploys tokens for the blockchain network in the V-Chain ecosystem. 4. Service Portals and APIs V-Chain provides the main communication method through REST API and Web/Portal.

content: BKSign Home BKSign The Problem As technology develops, working from home and remote work have become increasingly common. As a result, organizations and institutions are required to send documents in PDF format more frequently. This leads to a common issue: PDF documents often lack the signature of the creator or an authorized person, reducing the authenticity of the document. Printing out documents for manual signing is time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address this, digital signatures were introduced. However, traditional methods like USB tokens or smart cards have shown limitations in today's context: high costs, inconvenience due to the need to carry physical signing devices, and suboptimal security. Remote Signing Remote signing is emerging as the next generation of digital signatures. It overcomes the limitations of traditional methods by freeing users from having to carry physical signing devices. With just familiar devices like smartphones, tablets, or laptops, users can securely and conveniently sign digital documents. BKSign - Internal Digital Signing Solution The BKSign internal digital signing solution, developed by the BKFintech team, addresses internal document management challenges faced by institutions and organizations — such as the need to sign various documents, certificates, diplomas, and having multiple signers with high volume, all while keeping deployment costs low. To achieve this, BKSign has implemented an internal Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) to issue internal digital certificates to users within the organization, instead of requiring users to purchase costly public digital certificates. content: eDiploma Home eDiploma The Problem Diplomas, certificates, and attestations are credentials typically issued by educational institutions or organizations to learners upon completion of a specific training program. Traditionally, these credentials are issued once in paper form, containing information about the learner, the training program, and the signature of the head of the issuing organization. As such, they are special documents of great significance and importance, meant to be carefully preserved for life. Today, fake diplomas and certificates have become a growing issue in society. With minimal cost, individuals can easily obtain counterfeit documents that are marketed as difficult to detect. The verification process for these credentials is often lengthy, inconvenient, and potentially costly, allowing fake documents to persist in our society. To address this problem, it is essential to provide learners with an additional digital credential that contains authenticated information and is easy to verify. Our Solution eDiploma is a powerful solution that enables organizations and educational institutions to issue digital versions of diplomas, certificates and credentials. These digital documents are legally valid and easy to verify. Powered by digital signature technology, eDiploma ensures the authenticity of the signer and the integrity of the document. Key Features of eDiploma: High-speed digital signing: eDiploma’s digital signing system stands out with its exceptional signing speed, capable of processing 15,000 files per minute, meeting the demand for high-volume digital signing in a short period of time. This is especially crucial for events where a large number of certificates need to be issued immediately

This enables organizations to efficiently handle large batches of certifications, minimizing processing time while ensuring accuracy and consistency for every certificate issued. Flexible signing integrations: The system also supports a wide range of digital signing methods, allowing integration with multiple Certificate Authorities (CAs). This flexibility enables users to choose the signing method that best fits the specific requirements and conditions of their organization. Intuitive and user-friendly interface: eDiploma offers a convenient and intuitive certificate template configuration feature, with a simple setup process and the ability to reuse previously created templates. Users can define a template once and reuse it across multiple issuance batches, helping to save both time and effort in the management process. The template management interface is user-friendly, allowing for flexible editing and live preview, ensuring that each certificate meets both aesthetic and content requirements.

BKOffice is a testament to the “Made in Bach Khoa” philosophy — purpose-built to meet internal demands while maintaining the flexibility to adapt to future changes. It marks a critical milestone in HUST’s strategy toward comprehensive digital transformation.

content: WORKSHOP: APPLYING AI IN IDEA RESEARCH AND PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT Event Information • Time: 18:00 – 20:00, April 8, 2026 • Venue: HUST Building – MB Digital Hub, Hanoi University of Science and Technology • Registration: https://forms.gle/YHw7QXAWWtHmqMCu7 Program Overview As part of the supporting activities for participants of BK Fintech Hackday Batch 8, the workshop “Applying AI in Idea Research and Product Development” is organized to equip students with practical approaches and tools to effectively develop technology-driven ideas. The program addresses a common challenge faced by hackathon participants: how to move from an initial idea to a well-developed product within a limited timeframe. Through this workshop, participants will explore how AI can be applied across different stages of the product development process. Specifically, the workshop will focus on: • Applying AI in market research to identify user needs and key touchpoints • Using AI to rapidly design and develop product prototypes • Optimizing user experience through modern AI tools Beyond delivering knowledge, the workshop provides practical perspectives that help participants shorten development cycles and enhance their ability to turn ideas into competitive products in a hackathon environment. The program is expected to serve as a valuable support platform, enabling participants to approach BK Fintech Hackday Batch 8 with greater confidence while fostering innovation and the effective application of technology in practice.

content: Workshop Data Analytics in Marketing With the special participation of two experts from LEAD Consulting, the Data Analytics for Marketing Workshop provided attendees with valuable insights into the role and practical applications of data analytics in the field of marketing. Speakers & Contents Mr. Dang Tran Duc Minh (Co-founder, Director of Marketing & Business Development, LEAD Consulting) offered a comprehensive overview of how data drives modern marketing—from analyzing customer behavior to forecasting market trends. Notably, he introduced the Marketing Mix Modelling approach, a powerful tool for optimizing marketing budgets, identifying the most effective media channels, and measuring the impact of each marketing element on sales performance. Mr. Do Hoang Minh (Data Analyst, LEAD Consulting) shared practical techniques for data visualization and customer segmentation models such as RFM and K-Means. These models help businesses unlock the full potential of their data, enhance advertising strategies, and improve customer experience. Key Takeaways The workshop was not only a great opportunity for learners to acquire new knowledge but also a chance to connect with leading professionals in the field: 🔹Participants were introduced to real-world methods and widely-used tools in marketing data analytics. 🔹The workshop atmosphere was lively, with engaging discussions and thoughtful questions, reflecting strong interest in data-driven marketing. 🔹Most importantly, the real-world case studies shared by the experts gave participants a clearer understanding of how to apply data analytics to real business marketing strategies. content: Workshop Data Analytics in E-commerce On the afternoon of August 4, 2024, BK Fintech successfully hosted the Workshop: Data Analytics in E-commerce, featuring an insightful session on AI and Big Data applications in the e-commerce industry. The workshop was led by Mr. Tran Minh Tuan, Co-founder and CEO of Data Science JSC, the company behind Metric – a pioneering platform for e-commerce data intelligence in Vietnam. Speaker & Content In the first part of the session, Mr. Tuan introduced foundational concepts and key AI problems, including Classification, Regression, Structured Prediction, Clustering, Reinforcement Learning, Text Generation. These concepts form the foundation for understanding real-world AI applications, especially within the e-commerce landscape. In the second part, he provided deeper insights into the integration of AI and Big Data in customer data analysis. A highlight was the practical application of the RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) model, showcasing how data helps e-commerce businesses segment customers and optimize marketing strategies effectively. Key Takeaways Participants gained an understanding of core AI concepts and models relevant to e-commerce Real-world use cases illustrated how Big Data and AI drive decision-making in digital retail The workshop encouraged active discussion and interaction between participants and the guest speaker, creating a valuable bridge between academia and industry Moments from the Workshop The audience at the Data Analytics in E-commerce Workshop A participant asks a question during the Q&A session

content: CONFERENCE ON DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY AND ECONOMY (ECOTECH 2026) “DATA & AI: FROM INFRASTRUCTURE TO REAL-WORLD VALUE” ECOTECH is an annual conference jointly organized by the Institute for Digital Technology and Economy, Hanoi University of Science and Technology, and the Vietnam Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (VIASM). The conference serves as a platform connecting academia, industry, and the technology community in the fields of data, AI, and digital transformation. In 2026, ECOTECH officially returns with the theme: “Data & AI: From Infrastructure to Real-World Value” As data is increasingly recognized as a new production asset of the digital economy under Resolution No. 57-NQ/TW, Vietnam has been actively advancing key national initiatives such as the National Population Database, Project 06, and the National AI Strategy toward 2030. However, building infrastructure is only the beginning. The greater challenge lies in transforming data and AI into tangible value in governance, production, and services. With the goal of fostering dialogue among academia, enterprises, the data community, and legal experts, ECOTECH 2026 will bring together leading scientists, industry leaders, and experts in data and artificial intelligence to discuss: National data and AI infrastructure AI applications in enterprises and real-world operations Transforming data into economic value Legal frameworks and data governance in the digital era Speakers Ms. Nguyen Thi Ngoc Dung – Chief of Office, National Data Association Mr. Nguyen Trong Khang – Chairman and CEO, MK Group Dr. Ho Quoc Tuan – University of Bristol, United Kingdom Prof. Ho Tu Bao – AI and Data

content: ← Back to Conference PROF. DR. HO TU BAO Vietnam Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics ABOUT Prof. Ho Tu Bao is the Director of the Data Science Lab at the Vietnam Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (VIASM) and a Professor Emeritus at the Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (JAIST), where he served as a Professor and the Head of the Machine Learning and Data Mining Lab from 1993 to 2018. He earned his Bachelor's degree in Applied Mathematics from Hanoi University of Technology (1978), a Master of Science (1984), and a PhD (1987) in Artificial Intelligence from Pierre and Marie Curie University. In 1998, he completed his Habilitation à Diriger des Recherches at Dauphine University in France. His primary research focuses on machine learning methods and their applications in medicine and other fields. His academic interests also encompass digital transformation, teaching mathematics, and integrating AI into various domains of education and the economy. Recently, he published the book “AI và Con người” for the public readers and serves as a member of the National Advisory Council on Science and Technology, Innovation, and Digital Transformation.

content: LAUNCH OF HACK CX IN BANKING TOGETHER 2026 Hack CX in Banking Together 2026 has officially launched, offering a dynamic platform for young talents passionate about Fintech to tackle real-world challenges in the banking and financial sector. The competition aims to foster innovative, technology-driven solutions that enhance Customer Experience (CX) in banking, while providing participants with opportunities to develop critical skills, strengthen innovative thinking, and connect with industry experts. Participation Guidelines Each team consists of 3 to 5 members, collaborating to design and develop technology-based solutions addressing practical challenges in Fintech. Detailed information is available in the official participant handbook. Highlights of HACK <CX> TOGETHER 2025 In just 19 days of registration (from May 18 to June 5), the competition received applications from 106 teams with nearly 170 innovative ideas — far exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strong appeal and wide-reaching impact of the event in the tech and student communities nationwide. After a rigorous selection process, the Top 24 teams were chosen to enter the Mentoring Round. Over seven days, teams worked closely with nearly 60 industry experts from Techcombank, HUST, Lead Consulting, AWS, and other partners to refine their ideas. They then advanced to the 36-hour Hackathon Round, where they coded, designed, and presented their solutions with ongoing expert guidance, turning ideas into real, testable prototypes. content: BK Fintech Về chương trình Tài liệu học tập Tin tức Video Liên hệ Về chương trình Kinh tế số phát triển nhanh chóng đã và đang mở ra nhiều cơ hội tăng trưởng, đổi mới mô hình kinh doanh và mở rộng thị trường cho các doanh nghiệp, nhưng đồng thời các doanh nghiệp phải đối mặt với không ít thách thức, đặc biệt là các rủi ro liên quan đến an toàn, an ninh mạng. An ninh mạng – nền tảng vững chắc để tăng trưởng trong nền kinh tế số Trong bối cảnh Việt Nam thúc đẩy tăng trưởng kinh tế bền vững gắn với chuyển đổi số, việc triển khai hiệu quả Nghị quyết số 57-NQ/TW ngày 22/12/2024 của Bộ Chính trị về đột phá phát triển khoa học, công nghệ, đổi mới sáng tạo và chuyển đổi số quốc gia đã đặt ra yêu cầu cấp thiết về nâng cao năng lực an ninh mạng cho doanh nghiệp. Nhận thức rõ điều này, các hoạt động trong khuôn khổ dự án được triển khai nhằm hỗ trợ doanh nhân nữ chủ động nắm bắt cơ hội từ nền kinh tế số, đồng thời nâng cao năng lực nhận diện và ứng phó hiệu quả với những thách thức trên môi trường số. Khẳng định vị thế và quyền năng kinh tế của phụ nữ Việt Nam Hiện nay doanh nghiệp do phụ nữ làm chủ chiếm khoảng 24% tổng số doanh nghiệp của Việt Nam.

Các doanh nghiệp do phụ nữ làm chủ không chỉ đóng góp đáng kể vào tăng trưởng kinh tế và tạo việc làm, mà còn thể hiện vai trò tiên phong trong chăm lo đời sống người lao động, tham gia các hoạt động cộng đồng và thúc đẩy bình đẳng giới trong kinh doanh. Rủi ro an ninh mạng Nhiều doanh nghiệp do phụ nữ làm chủ còn hạn chế nguồn nhân lực công nghệ, kỹ năng bảo mật thông tin và năng lực bảo vệ tài sản số trong môi trường trực tuyến. title: Vườn ươm Nhân lực An toàn thông tin trong nền kinh tế số - ĐH Bách khoa Hà Nội

content: khai Dự án hỗ trợ các doanh nghiệp do phụ nữ làm chủ nâng cao năng lực chuyển đổi số và bảo đảm an toàn thông tin, an ninh mạng với các mục tiêu trọng tâm: Nâng cao năng lực thích ứng Cung cấp thông tin, nâng cao nhận thức cho các nữ lãnh đạo doanh nghiệp về ứng dụng hiệu quả công nghệ số để nâng cao năng lực cạnh tranh. Trang bị kĩ năng số và an ninh mạng Giúp doanh nhân nữ tự tin vận hành doanh nghiệp trước các mối đe dọa trên không gian mạng. Góp phần hiện thực hóa mục tiêu quốc gia Thực hiện có hiệu quả các chủ trương của Đảng và Nhà nước trong phát triển kinh tế - xã hội, xây dựng đội ngũ doanh nhân nữ vững mạnh, có khả năng thích ứng linh hoạt trong kỷ nguyên số. “An ninh mạng – Hành trang quan trọng trên hành trình chuyển đổi số và phát triển doanh nghiệp”. Sự chuẩn bị bài bản về năng lực an ninh mạng hôm nay chính là bước đệm cho sự tăng trưởng an toàn, bền vững và vươn xa của các doanh nghiệp do phụ nữ làm chủ trong tương lai. content: KHỞI ĐỘNG DỰ ÁN CYBER CLINICS - “CHƯƠNG TRÌNH VƯỜN ƯƠM NHÂN LỰC AN TOÀN THÔNG TIN TRONG NỀN KINH TẾ SỐ Ở VIỆT NAM” Sáng nay, ngày 16/04/2026, Đại học Bách khoa Hà Nội chính thức công bố triển khai Dự án “Chương trình Vườn ươm Nhân lực An toàn thông tin trong nền kinh tế số ở Việt Nam”, tài trợ bởi Quỹ Châu Á (The Asia Foundation - TAF). Dự án được thực hiện dưới sự quản lý của Bộ Giáo dục và Đào tạo, từ tháng 4/2026 đến hết tháng 3/2027. Dự án được triển khai nhằm xây dựng và vận hành mô hình “Vườn ươm An toàn thông tin” (Cyber Clinic) tại Đại học Bách khoa Hà Nội, do Viện Công nghệ và Kinh tế số trực tiếp tổ chức thực hiện, hướng tới mục tiêu phát triển nguồn nhân lực an toàn thông tin chất lượng cao, gắn liền với nhu cầu thực tiễn của nền kinh tế số. Bài toán kết nối giữa đào tạo và thực tiễn Phát biểu khai mạc buổi lễ, PGS. Huỳnh Đăng Chính - Phó Giám đốc Đại học Bách khoa Hà Nội nhấn mạnh vai trò của việc kết nối giữa ba trúc chính: Các doanh nghiệp vừa và nhỏ; Nền tảng chuyển đổi số và Nguồn nhân lực trong lĩnh vực an toàn thông tin; trong đào tạo và phát triển công nghệ. Mô hình này đồng thời nằm trong mạng lưới khu vực, kết nối các trường đại học trải rộng trên 13 quốc gia nhằm chia sẻ kinh nghiệm và phát triển cộng đồng thực hành. content: THE INSTITUTE FOR DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY AND ECONOMY – HANOI UNIVERSITY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY ANSWERS VTV1 INTERVIEW ON DIGITAL ASSET IDENTIFICATION As electronic identification and the digital society increasingly form the foundation of modern governance, the need for transparency, authentication, and data standardization to ensure product traceability has become more evident than ever. On VTV1, the Institute for Digital Technology and Economy shared its approach and practical experience in deploying digital diplomas, certificates, and electronic documents through the BKOffice and eDiploma solutions at Hanoi University of Science and Technology. content: HUST-TALENT PROJECT General Introduction The Institute for Digital Technology and Economy, Hanoi University of Science and Technology, is seeking candidates who are leading experts from Viet Nam and abroad to apply for positions under the HUST-Talent Project. HUST-Talent is part of the strategic orientation to develop Hanoi University of Science and Technology into a leading research university in the region, contributing to the realization of Resolution No. 71-NQ/TW on the central role of higher education in developing high-quality human resources and promoting innovation. The Institute for Digital Technology and Economy was established with the mission of becoming a leading research institute nationwide, contributing to the development of the digital economy and digital society through research, development, and application of Industry 4.0 technologies. The establishment of the Institute also contributes to enhancing Hanoi University of Science and Technology’s capacity for multidisciplinary science and technology collaboration, as well as sharing resources and facilities among research groups. At the time of its establishment, the Institute involved researchers and learners from three main units of Hanoi University of Science and Technology, including the School of Information and Communication Technology; the School of Economics and Management; and the Department of Mathematics and Informatics. Collaboration among research groups enables the resolution of complex problems requiring interdisciplinary approaches, arising from the fields of economics and finance, which demand the application of mathematical modeling and analysis while being implemented through information technology. content: WEBINAR: BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE – NỀN TẢNG CHUYỂN ĐỔI SỐ CHO DOANH NGHIỆP On November 12, the Institute for Digital Economy and Technology – Hanoi University of Science and Technology, in collaboration with Finxdemy – Technology Training and Consulting, organized the webinar “Business Intelligence – The Digital Transformation Platform for Enterprises,” attracting nearly 100 participants who were students, learners, and working professionals in the fields of technology, finance, and data. The speaker of the webinar, Dr. Pham Thi Nguyet Nga – Director of Data Governance and Analytics at OCB, and a Member of the Advisory Council of the Institute for Digital Economy and Technology, Hanoi University of Science and Technology – delivered an insightful, inspiring, and practical sharing about the development journey of Business Intelligence (BI) in enterprises. In her sharing, Dr. Nga helped participants gain a clearer understanding of: The BI Evolution: From Reporting to Intelligence – the shift from merely “reporting the past” to “predicting and automating the future.” BI as the foundation of digital transformation, helping enterprises make decisions more proactively, quickly, and accurately. BI is not only a tool but a data culture – where every decision is reflected through data. Case study: Customer Onboarding Process, illustrating how BI helps enterprises optimize processes and enhance customer experience through automation and real-time data analytics. Along with the message “Think big, do small & iterative” – Think big, start with small steps, and continually improve to create sustainable value from data. Webinar BI - Nền tảng chuyển đổi số
